@graph.comment: Mints the ID-JAGs (Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grants) the storages' authorization servers trade for access tokens. Signed with the Solid-OIDC key, so the existing `/.oidc/jwks` publishes the verification key. See docs/plans/lws-auth.md C1.

The access tokens of this OpenID provider are the LWS authentication credentials of its users: the UI and other clients of this server exchange them at the UAS below for ID-JAGs. Restricting them to this server (`aud` = `iss`) keeps them from being replayed at another authorization server; `cnf.jkt` (DPoP) proves possession on top of that. Solid-OIDC deployments keep the default `solid` audience.

Verifies the authentication credential presented at this UAS. `trustedIssuers` is this server, so the subject document is not dereferenced. Two shapes are accepted: access tokens of the OpenID provider of this server (`aud` = this server, `cnf.jkt` from DPoP), and the self-issued `at+jwt` of the agent/authorization-agent suite (`aud: solid`, `cnf.jkt`). A token with `cnf.jkt` is only accepted together with a DPoP proof for that key, and `requireRestrictedTokens` refuses unbound tokens whose audience is not this server.
Accepts an incoming ID-JAG at a UAS for the C2 impersonation hop (Bob -> YoYo). The signature/audience/claim are verified before the handler re-issues it under the visible subject.
Independent UAS check (C4): an incoming delegated ID-JAG claim must match a grant the assigner issued and stores in their own grant registry before this UAS re-issues it.
LWS token endpoint of the UAS: exchanges an ID token (optionally DPoP-bound) for an ID-JAG restricted to one storage's authorization server.
